BACKPORT: media: staging/intel-ipu3: parameter buffer refactoring Current ImgU driver processes and releases the parameter buffer immediately after queued from user. This does not align with other image buffers which are grouped in sets and used for the same frame. If user queues multiple parameter buffers continuously, only the last one will take effect. To make consistent buffers usage, this patch changes the parameter buffer handling and group parameter buffer with other image buffers for each frame. Each time driver will queue one more group of buffers when previous frame processed and buffers consumed by css. Signed-off-by: Tianshu Qiu <tian.shu.qiu@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Bingbu Cao <bingbu.cao@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Sakari Ailus <sakari.ailus@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Mauro Carvalho Chehab <mchehab+samsung@kernel.org> (cherry picked from commit 8ecc7c9da013e702aa889002e1288521d7533293 git://linuxtv.org/media_tree.git master) BUG=b:139647343 TEST=Sanity checked basic camera functions. arc: networkd: Move setup and teardown logic into ArcService. This patch refactors the setup/teardown, init/uninit and enable/disable code from ArcIpConfig into ArcService. Earlier attempts to break each logical unit into multicle CLs caused too many problems given the timing and interconencted nature of these pieces, due largely to the fact that the functionality was beig split across processes. Another key change in this patch is the gating of enable/disable on both sides of the veth pair being up. This is achieved by DeviceManager listening to rt netlink messages on the host and ArcService doing the same in the container's net namespace. Doing so, guarantees that once IPv6 route detection and address assignment runs, it can set up the datapath and configuration immediately. One caveat here is that the device keeps state that is currently specific to the ARC guest alone. This will have to be expanded, if necessary, to accomodate others. More functionality is moved into Datapath from ArcIpConfig. In order to add DeviceManager unit testing, a base class was added for mocking. ArcIpConfig unit test removed since it is no longer relevant. hwid service: change endpoint to appspot.com. Due to the deprecation of Apiary at the end of 2019, the endpoint of hwid service is changed from googleplex.com (proxied to googleapis.com) to appspot.com. This commit uprevs the endpoints library to Cloud Endpoints v2 framework and change the `base_path` of API from `/_ah/[s]pi/` to `/api/`. Also the auth check is removed since the requests for appspot.com are not proxied from googleapis.com which auto sets the client identity to apiserving@prod.google.com. However, from the point of view of API clients, they just use an API key and are able to connect API endpoints without any further authentication. The original API protection is like a second layer of protection but not strongly required.
